newsitem.title: USA: December retailer sales grow, but don't excite.
newsitem.headline: December retailer sales grow, but don't excite.

text.p: Sales over the holiday shopping season generally met expectations, store chains said Thursday, but analysts said retailers' profits for the key fourth quarter would probably be a mixed bag.
Salomon Brothers said its index of sales at comparable stores rose 6.2 percent in December, up from a 3.9 percent gain in November and a 1.8 percent rise in December 1995.

The investment firm's research analysts said December sales varied significantly among discount stores, luxury retailers and department stores. "On balance, we believe sales were modestly below expectations for the month," they wrote in a research note.
Analysts said the five fewer shopping days between Thanksgiving and Christmas hurt results at stores open at least a year.
Sears, Roebuck and Co. was one of the better performers during the month, analysts said. The giant retailer, based in Hoffman Estates, Ill., said comparable-store sales rose 9.5 percent in December.
Sears Chairman Arthur Martinez told CNBC television that gross profits looked very favourable for December and the fourth quarter.

"The major retailers continue to gain market share," said Michael Niemira, analyst with Bank of Tokyo/Mitsubishi Ltd. "Even within the Sears report, they talk about the electronics area being one of the stronger areas," he noted, while that area was weak for speciality retailers.
"Over the past year or so, you have seen department stores pick up share from apparel speciality stores," said Karen Sack, an analyst with S & P Equity Group.
Among clothing stores, Limited Inc. said comparable-store sales fell 1 percent in December and it expected earnings for the year to fall slightly below Wall Street estimates.
Paul Harris Stores said its comparable-store sales rose 23 percent in December, continuing a turnaround at the once-troubled speciality women's clothing retailer.
Pier 1 Imports Inc., a Fort Worth, Texas-based furniture and gift retailer, reported a 16.8 percent gain.
Analysts said that overall discounting was not higher than planned during the holiday season, pointing to healthy fourth-quarter profits for some retailers.
"When you look at the industry as a whole, the discounting wasn't probably more than planned for," Niemira said.
But Kmart Corp. said its margins were hurt by discounting.

"The holiday season continued to reflect consumer demand for value-priced merchandise," Chief Executive Floyd Hall said in a statement. "As a result, Kmart experienced ongoing gross margin pressure during December, resulting in rates that are below plan for the quarter to date."
Profit margins also remained low in the highly competitive consumer electronics market, analysts said.
"There's just no margins left in that business," Sack said.
Minneapolis-based superstore Best Buy Co. Inc. said comparable-store sales fell 5 percent in December, while Tandy Corp., based in Fort Worth, said its same-store sales also fell 5 percent.

"Sales were below company expectations as a result of the continued industry weakness in personal computers and consumer electronics," Best Buy Chief Financial Officer Allen Lenzmeier said in a statement.
"The anticipated January introduction of Intel's MMX microprocessor resulted in an extremely promotional environment and significantly lower selling prices of personal computers," he said.

Intel Corp. introduced its new chip on Wednesday and at least 20 computer makers and 19 software companies announced new products using the MMX Pentium, designed to enhance video, graphics and sound on personal computers.
While analysts said retail inventories were better managed this season than in the past, some said there still could be problems ahead.

"Some stores will report earnings improvement for the Christmas quarter, but through field research it is our opinion that the amount of winter merchandise still in the stores is a great liability and subsequent markdowns could severly impact earnings," Dillon, Read & Co. analyst Peter Schaeffer said in a research report.
Sears stock rose $1.375 to $46.625, Kmart added 50 cents to $11, and Dayton Hudson rose $1.50 to $37.875.
Best Buy fell 12.5 cents to $10.375, Limited fell 87.5 cents to $16.875 and Tandy was up 12.5 cents at $41.25.
